source: Wilie et al. (2024) Belief Revision: The Adaptability of Large Language Models Reasoning (Belief-R)
finding: Belief-R tests whether models drop a prior conclusion when a third premise defeats it (delta reasoning). 30 LMs tested. Most models almost never revise.
numbers: Small and non-API models: near 0% belief-update accuracy (BU-Acc). Eight large LLMs (Llama-3 70B, Mixtral 8x22B, Command R/R+, Claude 3 Haiku/Sonnet, GPT-3.5/4 Turbo): at most about 50% on BREU (mean of BU-Acc and BM-Acc).
limits: Logical premises only (modus ponens/tollens), single new premise as trigger; belief means the context-stated conclusion, not hidden states.
agent_relevance: Baseline: plain models are stale-belief keepers. A Revise state cannot rely on the model noticing a defeater by itself; the check result must be fed in explicitly.

source: Wilie et al. (2024) Belief Revision: The Adaptability of Large Language Models Reasoning (Belief-R) - update/maintain trade-off
finding: Models good at updating are bad at holding firm when no update is needed, and the reverse. Same setup, two subsets: Belief Update (BU) and Belief Maintain (BM).
numbers: Llama-3 70B direct prompt: BU 10.99%, BM 92.09%, BREU 51.54%. Models above 75% on basic inference at step t still lose accuracy on the BM subset (an irrelevant third premise acts as a distractor).
limits: Row labels in the appendix table are misaligned in the extracted text, so only the first model row is quoted with certainty.
agent_relevance: Measure both sides: track false revisions (over-flip) and missed revisions (inertia). Revising always or never both look fine on one metric.

source: Wilie et al. (2024) Belief Revision: The Adaptability of Large Language Models Reasoning (Belief-R) - prompting
finding: Chain-of-thought and plan-and-solve gave only marginal gains on belief revision; effects differ by model and by subset.
numbers: Average BREU gain from better prompting about 1 point. Per-model changes go both ways (some models gain over 10 points BU; Claude-3 Sonnet and GPT-4 Turbo lost with the same prompt). Modus tollens items give lower BREU than modus ponens.
limits: Zero-shot prompts only; 2024 models.
agent_relevance: Do not expect a thinking prompt to supply revision. Needs structure: explicit list of beliefs plus the new fact.

source: DeltaLogic (Dhanda 2026) Minimal premise edits reveal belief-revision failures in logical reasoning models
finding: Turns FOLIO and ProofWriter items into 4-turn episodes: answer, edit one premise, answer again. Edits: support insertion, defeating-fact insertion, support removal, irrelevant addition. Separates inertia, over-flip, abstention.
numbers: Qwen3-1.7B (n=30): initial 0.667, revised 0.467, inertia 0.600. Qwen3-4B (n=20): 0.650 to 0.450, inertia 0.600. Phi-4-mini (n=20): 0.950 to 0.850, inertia 0.200, over-flip 0.100, abstain 0.350. Qwen3-0.6B abstains 100%.
limits: Tiny (100 episodes built, 20-30 per model), log-likelihood label scoring, no CoT, small models only, workshop paper.
agent_relevance: Retraction cases (support removal, defeater) fail far more than additions. Qwen3-1.7B scored perfect on support insertion and 0 on removal and defeater edits. Our Revise state must test retraction explicitly.

source: DeltaLogic (Dhanda 2026) Minimal premise edits reveal belief-revision failures in logical reasoning models - edit-type asymmetry
finding: Adding a supporting premise is easy; losing support or receiving a defeater is hard. Scale (1.7B to 4B) did not fix inertia.
numbers: Qwen3-4B 0.000 revision accuracy on ProofWriter support-removal; Phi-4-mini 0.667 on the same.
limits: Same small sample. Stated as evidence of the failure mode, not a leaderboard.
agent_relevance: Matches AGM contraction being harder than expansion: dropping a belief needs knowing what depended on it.

source: Chowdhury (2026) Commitment Hierarchies under Intent Revision: A Belief-Revision Account of Salvage in Tool-Use Agents
finding: Treats a user changing the task as an AGM-style revision of a plan DAG. Each cached sub-result is keep, patch or discard. Asking a model node by node is unreliable; classifying the revision once and propagating by a deterministic pass reaches the oracle.
numbers: CostBench 1,080 instances: per-node gpt-4o judge recovers 0.44 of oracle savings (zero over-salvage); structured judge 1.00 on templated (60/60), 0.90 [0.86,0.95] when paraphrased (140/150). Keep-all reuses stale results on all 360 full-swap revisions (67% correct). Oracle cost 67.95 vs restart 119.15 (43% cheaper).
limits: Own formal postulates (Success, Inclusion, Vacuity, Consistency, Minimality), no AGM representation theorem claimed; provenance must be recorded by the executor.
agent_relevance: Direct design lesson for S5: record per step which constraint it read (provenance), classify the failure once, then propagate staleness with plain code, not by asking the model per step.

source: Chowdhury (2026) Commitment Hierarchies - theorem and synthetic DAG
finding: Proves no policy that sees only a node's local view can be both safe (no stale reuse) and cost-optimal. Giving the model producer status helps safety but not savings.
numbers: Synthetic DAG, 188 instances: savings recovered per-node / informed / structured: gpt-4o 0.28/0.52/1.00; gpt-4o-mini 0.00/0.60/1.00; gemini-2.5-flash 0.04/0.15/1.00. Keep/discard-only with perfect labels recovers 0.76, so patch matters.
limits: Synthetic environments; claim is about information structure plus reliability, not general capability.
agent_relevance: Supports a three-way outcome (keep, patch, discard) rather than keep or rewrite from scratch.

source: Chowdhury (2026) Commitment Hierarchies - context reset on real rollouts
finding: Keeping the environment state but resetting the context to what is done and what remains beat keeping the full message history.
numbers: STT-Arena gpt-5 rollouts (n=120): full history kept 0.11 pass rate, same as restart 0.11; state kept with reset context 0.52; tool calls cut 41% on the both-pass subset (n=12).
limits: Small n; one model family; conflict authored by a model.
agent_relevance: Evidence that stale reasoning text in context anchors the agent. Revise should carry forward the surviving belief set, not the transcript.

source: Park (2026) Graph-Native Cognitive Memory for AI Agents: Formal Belief Revision Semantics (Kumiho)
finding: Maps AGM onto an agent memory graph: immutable revisions, a Supersedes edge replaces a belief, retrieval excludes superseded ones. Proves basic postulates K*2-K*6 at belief-base level, adds Hansson Relevance and Core-Retainment, and rejects Recovery on purpose.
numbers: Automated compliance test: 49 scenarios, 7 postulates, 100% pass. LoCoMo F1 0.447 (n=1,540); adversarial refusal 97.5% (n=446); LoCoMo-Plus 93.3% judge accuracy (n=401) with GPT-4o, 88% with GPT-4o-mini; independent reproduction by benchmark authors mid-80s%.
limits: Single-vendor, self-reported. Compliance tests check the implementation, not the LLM. Postulates K*7 and K*8 left open. Propositional ground triples only.
agent_relevance: Gives a working pattern: belief base plus supersede edges plus kept history. Recovery is rejected because archived content stays addressable, which is what an agent wants for best-so-far.

source: Chao et al. (2026) STALE: Can LLM Agents Know When Their Memories Are No Longer Valid?
finding: 400 expert-checked implicit-conflict scenarios (1,200 queries, up to 150K tokens): a later fact makes an earlier memory stale without negating it. Probes State Resolution, Premise Resistance, Implicit Policy Adaptation.
numbers: Best model Gemini-3.1-pro 55.2% overall; Qwen3.5-27B 31.3%; GPT-4o-mini 8.7%; most memory frameworks (Zep, A-mem, mem0, LightMem) under 18%. Premise Resistance near 0-4% for most models (Gemini-3.1-pro 30% and 14%). Qwen3.5-27B: 76.0% State Resolution but 39.0% Policy Adaptation (Type I).
limits: LLM judge (95.83% agreement with humans on 240 items); everyday-life topics; row labels in the table are partly shifted in text extraction.
agent_relevance: Recognising a belief is stale does not mean acting on it, and models accept a question that presupposes the stale belief. Revise must propagate to dependents and check follow-up steps for stale premises.

source: Chao et al. (2026) STALE - CUPMEM adjudication
finding: Write-time state adjudication (consolidate the state, search for dependent slots, block stale premises at read time) lifts the same backbone.
numbers: GPT-4o-mini backbone: overall 8.7% to 68.0%. Premise Resistance 78.0% (Type I) and 75.0% (Type II). Cost about $0.37 per instance. Implicit Policy Adaptation only 32.0% and 43.0%.
limits: Authors built the prototype on their own benchmark; fixed slot schema; multi-step cascades still hard.
agent_relevance: An explicit adjudication step before answering beats a bigger model. Same shape as S5 deciding before S6.

source: Singh (2026) When Does Belief-Based Agent Memory Help? (Nous)
finding: A Bayesian per-fact belief memory is inert on ordinary LoCoMo (no contradictions to resolve) but wins when sources differ in reliability.
numbers: LoCoMo 3-conversation subset: Bayesian update equals last-write-wins. Controlled contradiction/staleness benchmark: 100 vs 67 for last-write-wins, 100 vs 90 for LLM-over-raw-memory, 46 for frequency count. Content-inferred trust can be gamed (a confident poison earned reliability 0.96); provenance-capped trust min(provenance, content) fixes it.
limits: Synthetic contradiction benchmark; LoCoMo judge disagreement (59.97 vs 32.45 on identical outputs).
agent_relevance: Entrenchment should come from source provenance and test results, not from how confident the text sounds.

source: Wang (2026) TOKI: A Bitemporal Operator Algebra for Contradiction Resolution in LLM-Agent Persistent Memory
finding: Shows four production conflict rules (last-writer-wins, evidence-weighted, await-confirmation, per-rule policy) each admit named write anomalies. LLM judges add replay inconsistency, belief-drift skew, audit erasure. Keeps the losing fact in an audit row.
numbers: Cites BeliefShift: up to 42% of cross-session contradictions unresolved across seven model families. Audit-row defence moves LoCoMo accuracy by 0.86 on its one natural slice; ablating the typed memory layer removes 0.49 accuracy on 1,444 answerable questions.
limits: Mostly theory (soundness theorems); cross-system comparison stated as underpowered.
agent_relevance: Log the judge's decision with a key so a re-run gives the same winner; never erase the loser (supports keep-best-so-far).

source: Myakala et al. (2026) BeliefShift: Temporal Belief Consistency and Opinion Drift in LLM Agents
finding: 2,400 annotated multi-session trajectories; seven models, zero-shot and RAG. Models that follow users resist drift poorly; factual models miss legitimate updates.
numbers: RAG raised Belief Revision Accuracy by +0.09 on average and Contradiction Resolution by +0.07 but Drift Coherence only +0.02. GPT-4o with RAG: BRA 0.83, DCS 0.61 (text says Claude 3.5 Sonnet has the highest DCS, 0.79 and 0.81).
limits: Opinion-style beliefs, not logic; per-cell numbers could not be cleanly read from the extracted table; independent authors, not peer reviewed.
agent_relevance: Retrieving the old belief does not fix drift. A stability-versus-adaptability trade-off, same as BU/BM in Belief-R.

source: Sadhu et al. (2026) DERELAB: Defeasible Reasoning and Confirmation Bias in LLMs
finding: Generated multi-turn belief-updating chats (default and inheritance reasoning) with verified truth each turn. Nine models accept congruent evidence and resist incongruent evidence.
numbers: 17 of 19 model-by-reasoning-type cells significant after Holm correction. GPT-5.1 BiasGap 0.935 (accuracy on weakening updates 3.5%, OR 891, CI 586-1498). Gemma-4-12B gap 0.082. Know-but-do-not-output: GPT-5-mini labels weakening turns correctly 95.4% yet entailment accuracy 20.3%; Llama-3.1-70B 85.1% vs 14.9%. Qwen3-32B default gap 0.670, 0.816 when question order is reversed.
limits: Synthetic graphs; 9 models; effect labels fall sharply when question order is reversed, so part of the correct labelling is scaffolded.
agent_relevance: The model can say the evidence weakens a claim and still keep the claim. Revise should derive the new belief state by rule from the effect label, not ask again.

source: Sadhu et al. (2026) DERELAB - anchoring and off-path
finding: Anchoring: in conversations where truth changes, models keep their first prediction. Irrelevant turns also move some models.
numbers: Default-reasoning anchoring: GPT-5.1 0.433, Qwen3-32B 0.483; Gemma-4-31B and GPT-5-mini under 5%. Inheritance anchoring Gemma-4-E4B 0.635. Llama-3.1-8B intrudes on 36.2% of easy off-path turns (irrelevant evidence changes its answer).
limits: Same paper, same caveats.
agent_relevance: Both inertia and spurious flips are present, so a revision rule needs a relevance check first.

source: Zeng and Zhang (2026) LLMs exhibit unreliable updating of clinical judgment as patient evidence evolves
finding: Showing a model its own previous assessment shifts its next estimate but does not improve it. Matched ICU trajectories from health records.
numbers: 4,580 post-initial snapshots: longitudinal predictions 9.50 points higher than independent (mean absolute difference 14.90). Context raised absolute error in 46.20% of cases, lowered in 30.28%. AUROC 0.545 vs 0.541; Brier 0.281 to 0.284. Raising supplied prior from 10% to 90% moved the update by 26.2 points. Worsening evidence moved risk +16.43/+30.86/+45.21 points (subtle/moderate/strong) vs improving -11.66/-18.72/-25.55.
limits: Eight models, ICU risk endpoint; asymmetry persisted after headroom normalisation at moderate and strong strength.
agent_relevance: Carrying forward the earlier answer is an anchor, not free memory. The best-so-far should be re-validated against current evidence, not just inherited.

source: Zeng and Zhang (2026) - prompts and evidence validation
finding: Telling the model to check evidence first or to doubt the earlier assessment reduced the pull to the prior but did not make updates more accurate. A rule that keeps only revisions backed by evidence worked, at a coverage cost.
numbers: Qwen3-8B: evidence-first prompt cut prior-directed shift by 1.41 points (CI 1.05-1.77) with no change in error (+0.07). Anti-anchoring prompt cut shift 1.31 but raised harmed share by 3.95 points and error by 0.39. EVLU-2 kept 258 of 3,503 nontrivial revisions and cut the harmful fraction by 13.51 points (vs random retention, P<0.001).
limits: One 8B model for prompt tests; label-free evidence rule specific to clinical features.
agent_relevance: Do not ask the model to be less anchored; filter revisions by an external evidence check (reliability versus coverage trade-off).

source: Sun et al. (2026) Accurate but Not Humble: Epistemic Humility in LLM Agents under Knowledge Conflict
finding: Four agents (for example Claude Code, OpenHands, Qwen-Agent, GPT-5) when retrieved evidence contradicts parametric belief. Scores Identify, Solve, Escalate. Agents notice early and drop the conflict later.
numbers: Highest-accuracy cells have lowest Solve (about 45% down to under 10%) and Escalate (about 38% down to under 10%). Claude Code Identify F1 90.0% on BrowseComp. OpenHands on GAIA 51.0% conflict-split accuracy but ignores the conflict on its wrong items. Conflict mentions peak in first 10% of trajectory. Humility prompt: GPT-5 Escalate 1.6 to 60.7 on MoNaCo with accuracy 30.1 to 23.2.
limits: Conflict and control splits use different questions; annotator agreement Fleiss kappa 0.49 (Identify) and 0.63 (Escalate).
agent_relevance: Detected conflicts must be written to a durable place (a revision log) or they decay. Prompting for humility buys escalation by paying accuracy.

source: Guo and Cui (2026) BeliefScope: Evidence-Driven Revision and Pressure-Induced Shifts in LLMs
finding: A 2x2 design (relevant evidence x directional pressure) separates a real update from social following around a fixed proposition. Qwen/Llama 36 families, Gemma3-12B in a 12-family check.
numbers: Model rankings changed with control choice, decoding (stochastic vs greedy) and response channel (probability, choice, action). Reduced pressure-following under instructions was sometimes real resistance and sometimes opposite-direction movement (reactance).
limits: Profiles are conditional on evaluation settings; open models only; synthetic validation; per-model effect sizes not extracted.
agent_relevance: Test Revise with a matched control: same claim, once with a real defeater and once with only an assertion. A flip on the second is bad revision.

source: Abtahi et al. (2026) MEDLEY-BENCH: Behavioural Metacognition and Belief Revision Under Social Pressure
finding: 35 models from 12 families on 130 instances compare solo answer, private self-review and revision after analyst arguments and consensus.
numbers: Evaluation-mapped composite lowest relative score in 30 of 35 models. Adversarial subset (11 models): sensitivity to inverted consensus labels from near zero to shifts of about +11.6 and +7.3 points (Mistral Small 3.1, Qwen3-8B). Human rubric study: 24 paired vignettes, composite difference 0.727 (CI 0.500-0.942); inter-reviewer weighted kappa 0.389, human-LLM 0.637.
limits: Proof-of-concept v1.0; authors flag judge severity and pipeline explanations; model size does not order scores.
agent_relevance: Private self-review is measurable and models differ widely in how easily a fake consensus moves them.

source: Hase et al. (2021) Do Language Models Have Beliefs?
finding: Treats model beliefs by logical consistency and builds belief graphs. Tests belief-updating methods (SLAG) that must be sequential, local and generalising. Early test of AGM-like properties on LMs.
numbers: Paraphrase consistency under 70% in tested models; off-the-shelf optimizers are strong baselines; SLAG update success FEVER 99.98, zsRE 84.73, Wikidata5m 74.57. Belief graphs show many nonsensical dependencies.
limits: Weight-editing setting with small BART/RoBERTa-sized models, not prompt-only agents; reading partial (abstract, intro, tables).
agent_relevance: If edits to one fact do not propagate to entailed facts, the stored set is not a consistent belief set. Argues for tracking dependencies outside the model.

source: Giannouris et al. (2026) MOIRA: Policy Memory and Belief Revision for LM Agents in Non-Stationary Pair Trading
finding: Agent keeps a compressed policy memory and separately a revisable belief about a pair relationship. Ablations remove belief update or lifecycle reselection. 11 models, 13 configurations, 75 sessions.
numbers: Removing global belief update: GPT-4.1-mini Beta return 30.6% to 23.4% (Sharpe 3.62 to 2.51); GPT-5.4-mini No-Beta 24.3% to 2.7% (Sharpe 2.79 to 0.41). Removing reselection (replacing a failing hypothesis): 30.6% to 2.8% and 24.3% to 15.4%. More updates or pair switches did not consistently help.
limits: Single market period, simulated trading, median-return runs; backbone-dependent.
agent_relevance: A concrete agent-loop case where dropping a failing hypothesis and replacing it matters more than adding memory. Revision benefits are backbone-dependent.

source: Thielscher and Son (2026) A Study of Belief Revision Postulates in Multi-Agent Systems
finding: Generalises AGM and iterated-revision postulates to multi-agent Kripke models used in epistemic planning; shows a full-meet operator satisfies all generalised AGM postulates and discusses why a richer event-model operator is hard.
numbers: Theory paper: no empirical numbers. Mentions LLMs only as motivation for planning over user beliefs.
limits: Formal; no LLM test.
agent_relevance: Background for multi-source settings; low priority for a single-agent schema.

source: Aravanis (2026) Machine Learning as Iterated Belief Change a la Darwiche and Pearl
finding: Recasts training of binary neural nets as a chain of belief-set changes. Full-meet change is too crude; lexicographic revision and moderate contraction satisfy Darwiche-Pearl iteration.
numbers: Theory: no empirical results.
limits: Binary feed-forward nets only; formal.
agent_relevance: A reason to pick lexicographic (newest evidence outranks) vs moderate (minimal prior shift) policies for iterated rounds.

source: Almeida and Casals (2026) From Doyle to AGM: A Survey and an Implementation Roadmap for Belief Change
finding: Traces belief change from Doyle's truth maintenance (1979) and de Kleer's ATMS (1986) to AGM. Says AGM presupposes entrenchment or selection functions but gives little on how to build them; LLM systems learn preferences rather than being handed an order.
numbers: Survey, no experiments. Notes ATMS can implement partial meet revision by enumerating maximal consistent assumption sets.
limits: Narrative review; its LLM section is prospective, not empirical.
agent_relevance: Our test-result-driven ordering of beliefs is the learned entrenchment the survey says AGM lacks; ATMS-style justification sets are the practical data structure.

source: Chowdhury (2026) and Park (2026) read together: practical lessons
finding: Both AGM-in-agents papers keep the postulates but drop the full machinery: belief base not closed set; Recovery rejected or ignored; propagation done by code over a dependency graph; the LLM is used once to classify.
numbers: Chowdhury: classify once gives 1.00 savings vs 0.28-0.00 per node. Park: 100% on 49 operational postulate tests.
limits: Neither tests a free-running coding or reasoning agent; both authored their own checkers.
agent_relevance: Design rule for the schema: keep beliefs as a small base with provenance; the LLM only classifies the input; code propagates.

source: Cross-benchmark synthesis of 2024-2026 LLM revision tests (Belief-R, DeltaLogic, DERELAB, STALE, BeliefShift)
finding: Five independent benchmarks show the same pattern: models keep stale beliefs when evidence retracts or defeats them, may flip on irrelevant additions, and recognise staleness better than they act on it.
numbers: Belief-R BU-Acc near 0-20% for most large models; DeltaLogic inertia 0.60; DERELAB GPT-5.1 3.5% correct on weakening updates; STALE best 55.2%, premise resistance mostly under 5%.
limits: Different tasks, scoring and model generations; numbers are not comparable across papers.
agent_relevance: Set Revise metrics: inertia rate, over-flip rate, propagation to dependents, and premise resistance.
